bullets.text: Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield of AI focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trains on labeled data to map inputs to known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Trains on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns or structures (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative rewards (e.g., robotics, gaming).
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust parameters.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split to train the model and evaluate its performance on unseen data.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, including noise, leading to poor generalization.
Underfitting: Model is too simple and fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: Predicts continuous output using a linear function.
Logistic Regression: Predicts probability of class membership for classification tasks.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data based on feature values, easy to interpret.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processes sensor data, makes decisions, and navigates safely.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Assess performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, MSE.
Cross-Validation: Ensures model generalizes well by training and testing on different data subsets.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance using techniques like grid search.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent data; labeled data collection can be challenging.
Interpretability: Many complex models are difficult to understand, problematic in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair or unethical outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues where models either learn noise or are too simplistic.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased integration into daily life, enabling smarter technologies across various industries.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential as the field progresses.
